data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's distinguishing criterion—identifying and justifying out-of-checklist anomalies—fails for tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes because such tasks typically have fully specified correct answers. If the checklist is comprehensive, as the target's own countercondition admits, there are no out-of-checklist anomalies. This makes the criterion inapplicable to a large class of the very tasks the problem concerns, leaving no evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes genuine gain from mere compliance for those tasks.
